units.zh: （文琮錫文收）

units.literal: Xu Yougong

units.zh: （商彥若）
units.en: (Shang Yanruo)
units.literal: (Shang Yanruo)

units.zh: 唐臨，字本德，京兆長安人。
units.en: Tang Lin, whose style was Bende, came from Chang'an in the capital district of Jingzhao.
units.literal: Tang Lin, style name Bende, was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

units.zh: 周內史瑾之孫。
units.en: He was the grandson of Tang Jin, who had served Zhou as Interior Secretary.
units.literal: He was the grandson of Jin, Interior Secretary of Zhou.

units.zh: 其先自北海內徙。
units.en: His family had originally come from Beihai and later moved into the interior.
units.literal: His forebears had moved inward from Beihai.

units.zh: 武德初，隱太子討王世充，臨以策進說，太子引直典書坊，授右衛率府鎧曹參軍。
units.en: Early in the Wude era, when the crown prince marched against Wang Shichong, Lin went to the camp with a strategic proposal. The prince took him into the crown prince's document office and made him a staff officer in the Right Guard's armor bureau.
units.literal: Early in Wude, the Hidden Crown Prince campaigned against Wang Shichong; Lin advanced a plan to persuade him; the Crown Prince brought him into the document office and appointed him Armor Section Administrator of the Right Guard's Rate Command.

units.zh: 太子廢，出為萬泉丞。
units.en: After the crown prince's fall, he was posted out as assistant magistrate of Wanquan County.
units.literal: When the Crown Prince was deposed, he was sent out to serve as Assistant Magistrate of Wanquan.

units.zh: 有輕囚久系，方春，農事興，臨說令可且出囚，使就畎畝。
units.en: Several minor offenders had been held a long time. Spring had come and farming was underway, and Lin urged the magistrate to release them temporarily so they could work their fields.
units.literal: There were light prisoners long detained; it was spring and farm work was rising; Lin urged the magistrate that the prisoners might temporarily be released to go to the fields.

units.zh: 不許。
units.en: The magistrate refused.
units.literal: He did not permit it.

units.zh: 臨曰：「有所疑，丞執其罪。」
units.en: Lin said, "If you have doubts, I will answer for this myself."
units.literal: Lin said: "If there is any doubt, the assistant magistrate will bear the guilt."

units.zh: 令移疾，臨悉縱歸，與之約，囚如期還。
units.en: The magistrate took sick leave, and Lin sent every prisoner home under bond to return on the appointed day—and they did.
units.literal: The magistrate took leave on grounds of illness; Lin released them all to return home and made an agreement with them; the prisoners returned on schedule.

units.zh: 再遷侍御史。
units.en: He was promoted again to Attending Censor.
units.literal: He was transferred again to Attending Censor.

units.zh: 大夫韋挺責著位不肅，明日，挺越次與江夏王道宗語，臨進曰：「王亂班。」
units.en: Grand Master Wei Ting had scolded an official for failing to stand in proper order. The next day Ting himself stepped out of rank to speak with Prince Daozong of Jiangxia, and Lin stepped forward: "Your Highness has disturbed the court order."
units.literal: Grand Master Wei Ting rebuked someone for not standing in rank with proper dignity; the next day Ting stepped out of order to speak with Prince Daozong of Jiangxia; Lin advanced and said: "The prince has disturbed the ranks."

units.zh: 道宗曰：「與大夫語，何至爾！」
units.en: Daozong said, "I was only speaking with the grand master—must it come to this!"
units.literal: Daozong said: "Speaking with the grand master—how does it come to this!"

units.zh: 臨曰：「大夫亦亂班。」
units.en: Lin replied, "The grand master has disturbed the order as well."
units.literal: Lin said: "The grand master also has disturbed the ranks."

units.zh: 挺失色，眾皆悚伏。
units.en: Ting turned pale, and everyone present shrank in silence.
units.literal: Ting changed color; the assembly all shrank in awe.

units.zh: 俄持節按獄交州，出冤系三千人。
units.en: Soon afterward he went to Jiao Prefecture with imperial credentials to review legal cases and secured the release of three thousand prisoners held on false charges.
units.literal: Soon, bearing credentials, he investigated cases in Jiao Prefecture and released three thousand persons wrongfully imprisoned.

units.zh: 累遷大理卿。
units.en: He rose through successive posts to Minister of Punishments.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Punishments.

units.zh: 高宗嘗錄囚，臨占對無不盡，帝喜曰：「為國之要在用法，刻則人殘，寬則失有罪，惟是折中，以稱朕意。」
units.en: Emperor Gaozong once held a prison review. Lin answered every case without omission, and the emperor was pleased: "Governing a state depends on how the law is applied. Harshness maims the people; excessive leniency lets the guilty go free. Only a balanced middle course can satisfy my intent."
units.literal: Emperor Gaozong once reviewed prisoners; Lin's replies left nothing unspoken; the Emperor rejoiced and said: "The key to governing the state lies in using the law: if severe, people are maimed; if lenient, the guilty escape—only by striking the mean can it match Our intent."

units.zh: 它日復訊，余司斷者輒紛訴不已，獨臨所訊無一言。
units.en: On another review day, prisoners judged by the other officials all pleaded and protested endlessly, but not one of those Lin had tried said a word.
units.literal: On another day when questioning was resumed, the other officials who decided cases all at once pleaded and complained without end; only those Lin had questioned had not a single word.

units.zh: 帝問故，答曰：「唐卿斷囚不冤，所以絕意。」
units.en: The emperor asked why. He answered, "Minister Tang's rulings are never unjust, so they have nothing left to say."
units.literal: The Emperor asked the reason; he replied: "Minister Tang's judgments of prisoners are not unjust, and therefore they have no further intent."

units.zh: 帝嘆曰：「為獄者固當若是。」
units.en: The emperor sighed and said, "This is how a judge ought to be."
units.literal: The Emperor sighed and said: "One who conducts prisons ought indeed to be like this."

units.zh: 乃自述其考曰「形如死灰，心若鐵石」雲。
units.en: He then wrote his own appraisal of Lin: "His form was like dead ashes, and his heart like iron and stone."
units.literal: He then himself set forth his appraisal, saying "form like dead ashes, heart like iron and stone," and so on.

units.zh: 永徽元年，拜御史大夫。
units.en: In the first year of Yonghui he was appointed censor-in-chief.
units.literal: In the first year of Yonghui, he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 蕭齡之嘗任廣州都督，受賕當死，詔群臣議，請論如法，詔戮於朝堂。
units.en: Xiao Lingzhi had once served as military governor of Guangzhou. Having accepted bribes, he was liable to death. The emperor ordered the ministers to deliberate and directed that he be judged according to law; an edict then ordered execution in the court hall.
units.literal: Xiao Lingzhi had once served as military governor of Guangzhou; having accepted bribes he was liable to death. An edict ordered the ministers to deliberate and directed judgment according to law; an edict ordered execution in the court hall.

units.zh: 臨建言：「群臣不知天子所以議之之意。
units.en: Lin memorialized: "The ministers do not understand the Son of Heaven's purpose in ordering deliberation.
units.literal: Lin memorialized: "The ministers do not understand the Son of Heaven's purpose in ordering deliberation.

units.zh: 在律有八。
units.en: The law provides for eight mitigating considerations.
units.literal: In the law there are eight.

units.zh: 王族戮於隱，議親也；
units.en: Royal kin are executed in seclusion out of consideration for kinship;
units.literal: Royal kin are executed in seclusion—consideration for kin;

units.zh: 刑不上大夫，議貴也。
units.en: punishment does not reach great officers out of consideration for noble rank.
units.literal: punishment does not reach great officers—consideration for nobility.

units.zh: 今齡之貪贓狼扈，死有餘咎。
units.en: Lingzhi's greed and corruption were wanton, and death would not have been excessive punishment.
units.literal: Now Lingzhi's greed and corruption were wanton; death would not have been excessive punishment.

units.zh: 陛下以異於它囚，故議之有司，又令入死，非堯、舜所以用刑者，不可為後世法。」
units.en: Yet Your Majesty treated him differently from other prisoners, had the responsible officials deliberate, and then ordered death—this is not how Yao and Shun applied punishment, and it must not become a precedent for later generations."
units.literal: Your Majesty treated him differently from other prisoners, had the responsible officials deliberate, and then ordered death—this is not how Yao and Shun applied punishment and must not become a precedent for later generations."

units.zh: 帝然之。
units.en: The emperor approved.
units.literal: The Emperor approved.

units.zh: 齡之，齊高帝五世孫，由是免死。
units.en: Lingzhi was a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor Gao of Qi and thus escaped death.
units.literal: Lingzhi was a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor Gao of Qi, and thus escaped death.

units.zh: 臨累遷吏部尚書。
units.en: Lin was eventually promoted to Minister of Personnel.
units.literal: Lin was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 初，來濟謫臺州，李義府謫普州，臨奏許祎為江南巡察使，張倫劍南巡察使。
units.en: Earlier Lai Ji had been banished to Taizhou and Li Yifu to Puzhou. Lin recommended Xu Yi as touring commissioner for the Jiangnan region and Zhang Lun for the Sword-South circuit.
units.literal: Earlier, Lai Ji had been demoted to Taizhou and Li Yifu to Puzhou; Lin memorialized that Xu Yi be made Jiangnan touring commissioner and Zhang Lun Sword-South touring commissioner.

units.zh: 祎與濟善，而倫與義府有隙。
units.en: Xu Yi was friendly with Lai Ji, while Zhang Lun was at odds with Li Yifu.
units.literal: Yi was on good terms with Ji, while Lun had a rift with Yifu.

units.zh: 武後常右義府，察知之，謂臨遣所私督其過，坐免官。
units.en: Empress Wu habitually favored Li Yifu. Learning of the appointments, she accused Lin of sending his own men to pursue Yifu's faults and had him removed from office.
units.literal: Empress Wu often favored Yifu; perceiving this, she said Lin had sent his private agents to pursue Yifu's faults, and he was dismissed on that account.

units.zh: 起為潮州刺史，卒，年六十。
units.en: He was later appointed prefect of Chaozhou, where he died at the age of sixty.
units.literal: He was raised up as Prefect of Chaozhou; he died at age sixty.

units.zh: 臨儉薄寡欲，不好治第宅。
units.en: Lin lived plainly with few desires and never built a grand residence.
units.literal: Lin was frugal and with few desires and did not like to build mansions.

units.zh: 性旁通，專務掩人過。
units.en: Broadly accomplished by nature, he made a point of concealing others' faults.
units.literal: By nature broadly accomplished, he devoted himself especially to covering others' faults.

units.zh: 見妻子，必正衣冠。
units.en: Even before his wife and children he always dressed with full propriety.
units.literal: When he saw wife and children, he always straightened cap and robes.

units.zh: 兄皎，武德初，為秦王府記室，從王征討，掌書檄。
units.en: His elder brother Jiao, early in the Wude era, served as recorder in the household of the Prince of Qin, followed the prince on campaign, and handled dispatches and proclamations.
units.literal: His elder brother Jiao, early in Wude, served as Recorder of the Prince of Qin's household; he followed the prince on campaigns and managed documents and proclamations.

units.zh: 貞觀中，官吏部侍郎。
units.en: During the Zhenguan reign he rose to Vice Minister of Personnel.
units.literal: In the Zhenguan era he served as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

units.zh: 先是，選集四時補擬，不為限。
units.en: Previously, civil-service selection assemblies for supplemental appointments had been held in all four seasons without fixed limits.
units.literal: Previously, selection assemblies for supplemental appointments occurred in all four seasons without limit.

units.zh: 皎請以冬初集，盡季春止，後遂為法。
units.en: Jiao proposed holding the assembly from early winter through late spring, and this later became standard practice.
units.literal: Jiao requested that the assembly gather at the start of winter and end at the close of late spring; afterward this became law.

units.zh: 終益州長史，贈太常卿。
units.en: He ended his career as chief administrator of Yizhou and was posthumously honored as Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: He ended as Chief Administrator of Yizhou and was posthumously given Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 子之奇，給事中。
units.en: His son Zhiqi served as Supervising Secretary.
units.literal: His son Zhiqi served as Supervising Secretary.

units.zh: 坐章懷太子屬徙邊。
units.en: He was implicated as an associate of Crown Prince Zhanghuai and banished to the frontier.
units.literal: He was implicated as an associate of Crown Prince Zhanghuai and was banished to the frontier.

units.zh: 後除括蒼令，與徐敬業起兵，誅。
units.en: Later appointed magistrate of Kuocang, he joined Xu Jingye's rebellion and was put to death.
units.literal: Later he was appointed Magistrate of Kuocang; he joined Xu Jingye in raising troops and was executed.

units.zh: 臨孫紹紹，神龍時為太常博士。
units.en: Lin's grandson Shaoshao served as an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices during the Shenlong era.
units.literal: Lin's grandson Shaoshao, in the Shenlong era served as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 遷左臺侍御史、度支員外郎，常兼博士。
units.en: He was promoted to Attending Censor on the Left Terrace and Vice Director of the Revenue Section, often while retaining his erudite post.
units.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor of the Left Terrace and Vice Director of the Revenue Section, often concurrently holding the erudite post.

units.zh: 韋庶人請妃、公主、命婦以上葬給鼓吹，詔可。
units.en: Empress Wei requested that imperial consorts, princesses, and titled ladies of rank and above be granted martial funeral music; the edict approved it.
units.literal: Consort Wei of Wei requested that consorts, princesses, and titled ladies of rank and above be granted martial music at burial; an edict approved it.

units.zh: 紹曰：「鼓吹本軍容，黃帝戰涿鹿，以為警衛，故曲有《靈夔吼》、《雕鶚爭》、《石墜崖》、《壯士怒》之類。
units.en: Shao objected: "Martial music was originally military ceremony. When the Yellow Emperor fought at Zhuolu he used it as a guard of honor, which is why the repertoire includes pieces such as 《Spirit Ao Roars》, 《Eagle and Hawk Contend》, 《Stone Falls from the Cliff》, and 《Warrior's Wrath》.
units.literal: Shao said: "Martial music was originally military bearing; the Yellow Emperor fought at Zhuolu and used it as guard and escort, and therefore the pieces include such titles as 《Spirit Ao Roars》, 《Eagle and Hawk Contend》, 《Stone Falls from the Cliff》, and 《Warrior's Wrath》.

units.zh: 惟功臣詔葬，得兼用之。
units.en: Only meritorious ministers granted burial by imperial edict were permitted to use it.
units.literal: Only meritorious ministers granted burial by edict might use it together.

units.zh: 男子有四方功，所以加寵。
units.en: It was a mark of honor for men who had rendered service on all four sides.
units.literal: A man who has merit on all four sides—therefore favor is added.

units.zh: 雖郊祀天地，不參設，容得接閨閫哉？
units.en: Even at the suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth it was not used—how then could it be extended to the women's quarters?
units.literal: Even at suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth it is not set up together—how could it be permitted to reach the inner quarters?

units.zh: 在令，五品官昏葬，無給鼓吹者，唯京官五品則假四品，蓋班秩在夫若子。
units.en: Under the statutes, fifth-rank officials were not granted martial music for weddings or funerals. Only capital officials of fifth rank might borrow fourth-rank privileges, because their rank followed that of husband or son.
units.literal: In the statutes, for fifth-rank officials' wedding and burial, none are given martial music; only capital officials of fifth rank borrow fourth rank, because their order and rank follow husband or son.

units.zh: 請置前詔，用舊典。」
units.en: I ask that the recent edict be withdrawn and the former regulations restored."
units.literal: I request that the previous edict be set aside and the old regulations used."

units.zh: 不省。
units.en: His plea went unheeded.
units.literal: It was not heeded.

units.zh: 中宗始郊，國子祭酒祝欽明等知韋後能制天子，欲迎諂之，即奏以皇后亞獻，安樂公主終獻，又四時及列帝誕日，遣使者詣陵如事生。
units.en: When Emperor Zhongzong first performed the suburban sacrifice, National University Libationer Zhu Qinming and others, knowing Empress Wei could dominate the emperor, sought to flatter her. They memorialized that the empress perform the secondary offering and Princess Anle the final offering, and that envoys be sent to the imperial tombs in all four seasons and on successive emperors' birth anniversaries as though the dead were still living.
units.literal: When Zhongzong first performed the suburban sacrifice, the National University Libationer Zhu Qinming and others, knowing that Empress Wei could control the Son of Heaven, wished to court and flatter her; they at once memorialized that the empress perform the secondary offering and Princess Anle the final offering; moreover, in all four seasons and on the birth days of successive emperors, they sent envoys to the tombs as if serving the living.

units.zh: 紹以為非禮，引正誼固爭。
units.en: Shao held these measures contrary to ritual and argued against them on principle without yielding.
units.literal: Shao regarded this as contrary to ritual and, citing orthodox principle, firmly contended.

units.zh: 帝又詔武氏陵及諸武墓皆置守戶，紹謂：「昊、順二陵守戶五百，與昭陵同。
units.en: The emperor also ordered guard households placed at the Wu clan tombs and all Wu family graves. Shao protested: "The tombs of Emperors Hao and Shun have five hundred guard households—the same as Taizong's Zhaoling.
units.literal: The Emperor also ordered guard households set at the Wu clan tombs and all Wu family graves; Shao said: "The tombs of Emperors Hao and Shun have five hundred guard households, the same as Zhaoling.

units.zh: 在令，先世帝王陵戶二十，今雖崇奉外家，宜準附常典。
units.en: The statutes prescribe only twenty guard households for the tombs of former emperors. Though the empress's kin are now honored, they should still follow the regular precedent.
units.literal: In the statutes, tombs of emperors of former ages have twenty guard households; though the maternal kin are now honored, they ought to follow and attach to the regular canon.

units.zh: 又親王墓戶十，梁、魯乃追贈，不可逾真王。
units.en: Princely tombs receive ten guard households. Liang and Lu were posthumous enfeoffments and cannot exceed true princes.
units.literal: Moreover, princely tombs have ten guard households; Liang and Lu were posthumous enfeoffments and cannot exceed true princes.

units.zh: 褒德衛卒，至逾宗廟，不可明甚，請罷之。」
units.en: To honor the Wu clan with guard troops that exceed even the imperial ancestral temple is plainly excessive. I ask that these orders be revoked."
units.literal: Honoring virtue with guard soldiers, yet reaching beyond the ancestral temple—this cannot be made clear enough; I request that it be abolished."

units.zh: 又言：「比群臣務厚葬，以俑人象驂眩耀相矜，下逮眾庶，流宕成俗。
units.en: He also said, "Lately officials compete in lavish funerals, displaying figurines and carved teams of horses in dazzling show, and the fashion has spread even among commoners.
units.literal: He also said: "Recently ministers have devoted themselves to lavish burial, using figurines and images of paired horses in dazzling display to vie with one another, reaching down to the common people until it has become a drifting custom.

units.zh: 願按令切敕裁損，凡明器不許列衢路，惟陳墓所。
units.en: I ask that the statutes be strictly enforced to curb this excess. Spirit goods should not be displayed on public roads but only at the burial site.
units.literal: I wish that according to the statutes a stern edict cut and reduce this; all spirit objects are not permitted to be arrayed on public roads, but only displayed at the tomb site.

units.zh: 昏家盛設障車，擁道為戲樂，邀貨捐貲動萬計，甚傷化紊禮，不可示天下。」
units.en: Wedding processions now fill the roads with barrier carts and public entertainments, extorting contributions that run to tens of thousands. This deeply corrupts morals and disrupts ritual. Such practices must not be displayed before the empire."
units.literal: Wedding families lavishly set out barrier carts, blocking the road for sport and amusement, soliciting goods and contributing wealth by the tens of thousands—greatly injuring transformation and disordering ritual; this cannot be shown to all under Heaven."

units.zh: 事雖不從，議者美嘆。
units.en: Though his proposals were not adopted, commentators praised him with admiration.
units.literal: Though the matters were not followed, those who discussed them praised and sighed in admiration.

units.zh: 睿宗即位，數言政損益，再遷給事中，兼太常少卿。
units.en: After Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he repeatedly offered advice on government policy and was twice promoted, becoming Supervising Secretary and concurrently Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he repeatedly spoke on what would benefit or harm government; he was transferred again to Supervising Secretary and concurrently Vice Minister of the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

units.zh: 先天二年，玄宗講武驪山，紹以典儀坐失軍容，當斬。
units.en: In the second year of Xiantian, when Emperor Xuanzong held martial exercises at Mount Li, Shao was charged with a breach of ceremonial protocol in military display and sentenced to death.
units.literal: In the second year of Xiantian, Xuanzong held martial exercises at Mount Li; Shao, for ritual management, sat in failure of military bearing and was liable to execution.

units.zh: 帝怒甚，執纛下，左右猶冀少貸，金吾將軍李邈遽傳詔斬之。
units.en: The emperor was furious. Shao was seized below the banner, and those nearby still hoped for some leniency, but Golden Crow General Li Miao immediately transmitted the execution order and had him beheaded.
units.literal: The Emperor was extremely angry; he seized the banner and came down; those at his side still hoped he might spare him somewhat, but the Golden Crow General Li Miao hastily transmitted the edict and executed him.

units.zh: 時深咎邈，帝亦悔，俄詔罷邈官，擯於家。
units.en: Many blamed Li Miao severely. The emperor himself soon regretted the affair and shortly dismissed Miao from office, banishing him to his home.
units.literal: At the time they deeply blamed Miao; the Emperor also repented, and soon an edict dismissed Miao from office and banished him to his home.

units.zh: 張文瓘，字稚圭，貝州武城人。
units.en: Zhang Wenqian, whose style was Zhigui, came from Wucheng in Beizhou.
units.literal: Zhang Wenqian, style name Zhigui, was a native of Wucheng in Beizhou.

units.zh: 隋大業末，徙家魏州之昌樂。
units.en: At the end of the Sui Daye era his family moved to Changle in Weizhou.
units.literal: At the end of Sui Daye, his family moved to Changle in Weizhou.

units.zh: 幼孤，事母、兄以孝友聞。
units.en: Orphaned in childhood, he was famed for the filial devotion and brotherly affection with which he cared for his mother and elder brother.
units.literal: Orphaned young, he served mother and elder brother and was known for filial piety and brotherly affection.

units.zh: 貞觀初，第明經，補并州參軍。
units.en: Early in the Zhenguan reign he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed military aide in Bingzhou.
units.literal: Early in Zhenguan he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Military Aide of Bingzhou.

units.zh: 時李勣為長史，嘗嘆曰：「稚圭，今之管、蕭，吾所不及。」
units.en: Li Ji was then chief administrator of the prefecture. He once sighed and said, "Zhigui is a Guan Zhong or Xiao He for our age—he surpasses what I can do."
units.literal: At the time Li Ji was Chief Administrator; he once sighed and said: "Zhigui is the Guan and Xiao of today—what I cannot match."

units.zh: 勣入朝，文瓘與屬僚二人皆餞，勣贈二人以佩刀、玉帶，而不及文瓘。
units.en: When Li Ji went to court, Wenqian and two subordinate officials all saw him off. Ji gave the two men girdle knives and jade belts but gave Wenqian nothing.
units.literal: When Ji entered court, Wenqian together with two subordinate officials all saw him off; Ji presented the two with girdle knives and jade belts, but did not include Wenqian.

units.zh: 文瓘以疑請，勣曰：「子無為嫌。
units.en: Wenqian asked about the omission. Ji said, "Do not take offense.
units.literal: Wenqian, puzzled, asked; Ji said: "Sir, do not take it as a slight.

units.zh: 若某，豫少決，故贈以刀，欲其果於斷；
units.en: One of them is hesitant by nature, so I gave him a knife to encourage firm decisions.
units.literal: As for so-and-so, he is by nature lacking in decisiveness, and therefore I gave him a knife, wishing him to be firm in judgment;

units.zh: 某放誕少檢，故贈以帶，俾其守約束。
units.en: The other is undisciplined and unrestrained, so I gave him a belt to keep him within bounds.
units.literal: so-and-so is unrestrained and lacking in restraint, and therefore I gave him a belt to make him keep to discipline.

units.zh: 若子才，無施不可，焉用贈？」
units.en: Your talent needs no such aid—why should I give you a gift?"
units.literal: As for your talent, there is nothing it cannot be applied to—why use a gift?"

units.zh: 因極推引。
units.en: He then strongly recommended Wenqian for advancement.
units.literal: He thereupon strongly recommended him.

units.zh: 再遷水部員外郎。
units.en: He was promoted again to Vice Director of the Water Section.
units.literal: He was transferred again to Vice Director of the Water Section.

units.zh: 時兄文琮為戶部侍郎，於制，兄弟不並臺閣，出為雲陽令。
units.en: His elder brother Wencong was then Vice Minister of Revenue. Regulations forbade brothers from serving together at court, so Wenqian was posted out as magistrate of Yunyang.
units.literal: At the time his elder brother Wencong was Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue; by regulation brothers did not serve together in the central offices, and he was sent out as Magistrate of Yunyang.

units.zh: 累授東西臺舍人，參知政事。
units.en: He was repeatedly appointed drafter of the Eastern and Western Terraces and joined in governing affairs.
units.literal: He was repeatedly appointed Drafter of the Eastern and Western Terraces and participated in knowing government affairs.

units.zh: 乾封二年，遷東臺侍郎、同東西臺三品，遂與勣同為宰相。
units.en: In the second year of Qianfeng he was made Vice Minister of the Eastern Terrace with third rank and became chief minister alongside Li Ji.
units.literal: In the second year of Qianfeng he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Eastern Terrace and Same Rank as the Three Offices of the Eastern and Western Terraces, and thus together with Ji became chief ministers.

units.zh: 俄知左史事。
units.en: He soon took charge of the Left Historian's office as well.
units.literal: Soon he was charged with the affairs of the Left Historian.

units.zh: 時高宗造蓬萊、上陽、合璧等宮，復征討四夷，京師養廄馬萬匹，帑瓘浸虛。
units.en: Emperor Gaozong was building the Penglai, Shangyang, and Hebi palaces, campaigning again on all frontiers, and maintaining ten thousand horses in the capital stables. The treasury was steadily drained.
units.literal: At the time Gaozong built the Penglai, Shangyang, Hebi, and other palaces, again campaigned against the four barbarians, and in the capital stabled ten thousand horses in the stables; the treasury stores were gradually emptied.

units.zh: 文瓘諫曰：「王者養民，逸則富以康，勞則怨以叛。
units.en: Wenqian remonstrated: "A ruler nourishes his people. When they are at ease they grow prosperous and secure; when overworked they resent and rebel.
units.literal: Wenqian remonstrated, saying: "A king nourishes the people: if at ease, they grow wealthy and secure; if labored, they resent and rebel.

units.zh: 秦、漢廣事四夷，造宮室，至二世土崩，武帝末年戶口減半。
units.en: Qin and Han both campaigned widely and built palaces on a vast scale—Qin collapsed under the Second Emperor, and by the end of Emperor Wu's reign the registered population had been cut in half.
units.literal: Qin and Han broadly undertook affairs on the four sides and built palaces, until the Second Emperor's collapse; in the late years of Emperor Wu the registered population was halved.

units.zh: 夫制治於未亂，保邦於未危。
units.en: Good government means ordering affairs before chaos arises and securing the state before danger appears.
units.literal: To establish order before disorder, to preserve the state before peril.

units.zh: 人罔常懷，懷於有仁。
units.en: The people have no fixed loyalty except to those who show them benevolence.
units.literal: The people have no constant resting place; they rest in one who has benevolence.

units.zh: 臣願撫之，無使勞而生怨。
units.en: I beg Your Majesty to cherish them and not drive them to labor until resentment arises.
units.literal: Your servant wishes to comfort them and not let labor give rise to resentment.

units.zh: 隋監未遠，不可不察。」
units.en: The fall of the Sui is still recent history. This warning cannot be ignored."
units.literal: Sui's mirror is not far off; this cannot but be examined."

units.zh: 帝善其言，賜繒錦百段，為減廄馬數千。
units.en: The emperor approved his advice, rewarded him with a hundred lengths of silk brocade, and reduced the imperial stables by several thousand horses.
units.literal: The Emperor approved his words, bestowed a hundred lengths of silk brocade, and reduced the stabled horses by several thousand.

units.zh: 改黃門侍郎，兼太子右庶子，又兼大理卿。
units.en: He was made Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate, concurrently Right Vice Heir Apparent of the crown prince, and also Minister of Punishments.
units.literal: He was changed to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate, concurrently Right Vice Heir Apparent, and again concurrently Minister of Punishments.

units.zh: 不旬日，斷疑獄四百，抵罪者無怨言。
units.en: Within ten days he resolved four hundred doubtful cases, and even those convicted had no complaint.
units.literal: In less than ten days he decided four hundred doubtful cases; those condemned had no complaint.

units.zh: 嘗有小疾，囚相與齋禱，願亟視事。
units.en: Once when he fell slightly ill, the prisoners together fasted and prayed that he would soon return to duty.
units.literal: Once when he had a minor illness, the prisoners together fasted and prayed, wishing him to resume office quickly.

units.zh: 時以執法平恕方戴胄。
units.en: At the time he was regarded, together with Dai Zhou, as a model of fair and lenient justice.
units.literal: At the time, for impartial and lenient enforcement of the law, he was paired with Dai Zhou.

units.zh: 後拜侍中，兼太子賓客。
units.en: He was later appointed Palace Attendant and concurrently Guest of the Crown Prince.
units.literal: Later he was appointed Palace Attendant, concurrently Guest of the Crown Prince.

units.zh: 諸囚聞其遷，皆垂泣，其得人心如此。
units.en: When the prisoners heard of his transfer they all wept. Such was the hold he had on people's hearts.
units.literal: When the prisoners heard of his transfer, they all wept; such was the way he won people's hearts.

units.zh: 性嚴正，未嘗回容，諸司奏議，悉心糾駁，故帝委之。
units.en: Stern and upright by nature, he never showed favoritism. He scrutinized and corrected memorials from every office, and the emperor relied on him accordingly.
units.literal: By nature stern and upright, he never turned his countenance; on memorials and proposals from all offices he diligently corrected and refuted, and therefore the Emperor entrusted affairs to him.

units.zh: 或時移疾，佗宰相奏事，帝必問與文瓘議未。
units.en: Whenever he was ill and other chief ministers presented business, the emperor always asked whether they had consulted Wenqian.
units.literal: Sometimes when he took leave for illness, when other chief ministers reported affairs, the Emperor always asked whether they had discussed it with Wenqian.

units.zh: 若不者，曰：「往共籌之。」
units.en: If they had not, he said, "Go consult together with him."
units.literal: If not, he would say: "Go deliberate with him together."

units.zh: 或曰：「已議。」
units.en: Or they would say, "We have already consulted."
units.literal: Or someone would say: "Already deliberated."

units.zh: 即皆報可。
units.en: The emperor then approved whatever they reported.
units.literal: Then all were reported as approved.

units.zh: 新羅叛，帝將出兵討之。
units.en: When Silla rebelled, the emperor prepared to send troops against them.
units.literal: Silla rebelled, and the Emperor was about to send troops to punish them.

units.zh: 時文瓘病臥家，自力請見，曰：「吐蕃盜邊，兵屯境未解，新羅復叛，議者欲出師，二虜俱事，臣恐人不堪弊，請息兵修德，以懷異俗。」
units.en: Wenqian was bedridden at home but forced himself to seek an audience. He said, "Tibetans are raiding the frontier and troops remain tied down there, while Silla has rebelled again. Some counsel sending armies on both fronts at once. I fear the people cannot bear such burdens. I beg Your Majesty to halt the armies and cultivate virtue to win over foreign peoples."
units.literal: At the time Wenqian lay ill at home; he forced himself to request an audience and said: "Tibetans are raiding the border, troops remain massed on the frontier without relief, and Silla has rebelled again. Those who discuss policy wish to send armies. With both barbarians engaged at once, your servant fears the people cannot bear the strain. I ask that arms be stilled and virtue cultivated to win over foreign peoples."

units.zh: 詔可。
units.en: The edict approved his request.
units.literal: An edict approved this.

units.zh: 初，同列以堂饌豐余，欲少損。
units.en: Earlier his colleagues, finding their official banquet provisions overly lavish, wished to cut them back.
units.literal: Earlier, colleagues because the hall provisions were abundant wished to reduce them somewhat.

units.zh: 文瓘曰：「此天子所以重樞務、待賢才也，吾等若不任職，當自引避，不宜節減，以自取名。」
units.en: Wenqian said, "The emperor provides these provisions to honor weighty state business and treat worthy officials. If we are not equal to our posts we should resign; we must not cut back to win praise for frugality."
units.literal: Wenqian said: "This is how the Son of Heaven shows weight to pivotal affairs and treats worthy talent. If we do not fulfill our duties, we ought to withdraw of ourselves; we should not cut expenses to win a reputation."

units.zh: 眾乃止。
units.en: The others dropped the proposal.
units.literal: The assembly then stopped.

units.zh: 卒，年七十三，贈幽州都督，謚曰懿。
units.en: He died at seventy-three, was posthumously made governor of Youzhou, and given the posthumous name Yi.
units.literal: He died at age seventy-three, was posthumously given Governor of Youzhou, and his posthumous title was Yi.

units.zh: 以嘗事孝敬皇帝，詔陪葬恭陵。
units.en: For having served Emperor Xiaojing, he was ordered buried at Gongling.
units.literal: Because he had once served the Filial and Respectful Emperor, an edict ordered him buried with honor at Gongling.

units.zh: 四子：潛，為魏州刺史；
units.en: He had four sons: Qian became prefect of Weizhou;
units.literal: Four sons: Qian served as Prefect of Weizhou;

units.zh: 沛，同州刺史；
units.en: Pei became prefect of Tong Prefecture;
units.literal: Pei, Tong Prefecture;

units.zh: 洽，衛尉卿；
units.en: Qia, commandant of the guards;
units.literal: Qia, Commandant of the Guards;

units.zh: 涉，殿中監。
units.en: and She, director of the palace directorate.
units.literal: She, Director of the Palace.

units.zh: 父子皆至三品，時謂「萬石張家」。
units.en: Father and sons all reached third rank, and contemporaries called them the "Zhang family of ten thousand stone."
units.literal: Father and sons all reached third rank; people of the time called them the "Wanshi Zhang family."

units.zh: 韋溫誅，涉為亂兵所殺。
units.en: When Wei Wen and his faction were killed, She died at the hands of mutinous troops.
units.literal: When Wei Wen was executed, She was killed by mutinous soldiers.

units.zh: 文琮，好自寫書，筆不釋手。
units.en: Wencong loved to copy books by hand and never put down his brush.
units.literal: Wencong loved to copy books by hand himself and never laid down his brush.

units.zh: 子弟諫止，曰：「吾好此，不為倦。」
units.en: When his sons and younger brothers urged him to rest, he said, "I enjoy this and never grow weary."
units.literal: When sons and younger brothers admonished him to stop, he said: "I delight in this and am not weary."

units.zh: 貞觀中，為治書侍御史，遷亳州刺史。
units.en: In the Zhenguan reign he served as attending censor for imperial documents and was promoted to prefect of Bozhou.
units.literal: In Zhenguan he served as Attending Censor for Imperial Documents and was transferred to Prefect of Bozhou.

units.zh: 永徽初，獻《文皇帝頌》，優制褒美，拜戶部侍郎。
units.en: In early Yonghui he presented an eulogy to Emperor Taizong; the emperor praised it in an edict and appointed him Vice Minister of Revenue.
units.literal: Early in Yonghui he presented Eulogy for Emperor Wen of Tang; an excellent edict praised him, and he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 坐房遺愛從母弟，出為建州刺史。
units.en: Implicated as a cousin of Fang Yiai, he was posted out as prefect of Jianzhou.
units.literal: He was implicated as maternal cousin of Fang Yiai and was sent out as Prefect of Jianzhou.

units.zh: 州尚淫祀，不立社稷，文琮下教曰：「春秋二社本於農，今此州廢不立，尚何觀？
units.en: The region still favored improper cults and had no state altars. Wencong issued an instruction: "The spring and autumn communal rites exist for farming, yet this prefecture alone has abandoned them. What example does that set?
units.literal: The prefecture still favored licentious sacrifices and did not establish the altars of soil and grain; Wencong issued an instruction, saying: "The two seasonal communal sacrifices of spring and autumn are fundamentally for agriculture; now this prefecture has abolished them and not established them—what is there to behold?

units.zh: 比歲田畝卒荒，或未之思乎！
units.en: In recent years the fields have often failed. Has no one considered why!
units.literal: In recent years the fields have often lain waste—has no one reflected on this!

units.zh: 神在於敬，可以致福。」
units.en: Spirits respond to reverence, and through reverence blessing may be won."
units.literal: The spirits lie in reverence; through it blessing may be attained."

units.zh: 於是始建祀場，民悅從之。
units.en: He then established the sacrificial ground, and the people gladly followed.
units.literal: Thereupon he first built the sacrificial ground, and the people gladly followed.

units.zh: 卒於官。
units.en: He died in office.
units.literal: He died in office.

units.zh: 子錫，久視初，為鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事，代其甥李嶠為宰相。
units.en: His son Xi, early in the Jiushi era, became vice minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and chancellor, succeeding his nephew Li Qiao.
units.literal: His son Xi, early in the Jiushi era, was Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Same Rank as the Three Offices of the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Tower, replacing his nephew Li Qiao as chancellor.

units.zh: 請還廬陵王，不為張易之所右。
units.en: He petitioned for the return of the Prince of Luling and earned the disfavor of Zhang Yizhi.
units.literal: He requested the return of the Prince of Luling and was not favored by Zhang Yizhi.

units.zh: 與鄭杲俱知選，坐泄禁中語，又賕謝鉅萬，時蘇味道亦坐事，同被訊，系鳳閣，俄徙司刑三品院。
units.en: He and Zheng Gao oversaw civil-service selection. For leaking palace secrets and accepting bribes of tens of thousands, he was investigated together with Su Weidao, detained in the Phoenix Pavilion, and soon moved to the Court of Punishments compound.
units.literal: Together with Zheng Gao he managed selection; for leaking palace speech and again bribing with tens of thousands, at the time Su Weidao was also implicated; together they were interrogated and held in the Phoenix Pavilion, soon moved to the Court of Punishments third-rank compound.

units.zh: 錫按轡專道，神氣不懾，日膳豐鮮，無損貶。
units.en: Xi rode the dedicated lane to detention unafraid, ate rich meals every day, and showed no sign of distress.
units.literal: Xi held the reins on the dedicated road, his spirit unafraid; daily meals were abundant and fresh, without reduction or demotion.

units.zh: 味道徒步赴逮，席地菜食。
units.en: Weidao walked to his arrest and sat on the ground eating plain vegetables.
units.literal: Weidao went on foot to be seized and sat on the ground eating plain vegetables.

units.zh: 武後聞之，釋味道，將斬錫，既而流循州。
units.en: Empress Wu released Weidao but was about to execute Xi; she then exiled him to Xunzhou instead.
units.literal: When Empress Wu heard this, she released Weidao and was about to execute Xi; presently she exiled him to Xunzhou.

units.zh: 神龍中，累遷工部尚書，兼修國史，東都留守。
units.en: During the Shenlong era he rose to Minister of Works, helped revise the national history, and served as defender of the eastern capital.
units.literal: In the Shenlong era he was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Works, concurrently revised the national history, and served as defender of the eastern capital.

units.zh: 韋後臨朝，詔同中書門下三品，旬日，出為絳州刺史。
units.en: When Empress Wei held court she made him chancellor of the third rank, but within ten days he was posted as prefect of Jiangzhou.
units.literal: When Empress Wei held court, an edict made him Same Rank as the Three Offices of the Secretariat and Chancellery; within ten days he was sent out as Prefect of Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 累封平原郡公，卒。
units.en: He was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan and eventually died.
units.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan and died.

units.zh: 文琮從父弟文收，終太子率更令。
units.en: Wencong's cousin Wenshou ended his career as commandant of the crown prince's rate-revision office.
units.literal: Wencong's paternal cousin Wenshou ended as Commandant of the Crown Prince's Rate Revision.

units.zh: 善音律，著《新樂書》十餘篇。
units.en: Skilled in music theory, he wrote New Music Writings in more than ten chapters.
units.literal: Skilled in pitch and mode, he authored New Music Writings in more than ten chapters.

units.zh: 徐有功，名弘敏，避孝敬皇帝諱，以字行，國子博士文遠孫也。
units.en: Xu Yougong, personal name Hongmin, avoided the taboo of Emperor Xiaojing and was known by his style; he was grandson of the National University erudite Xu Wenyuan.
units.literal: Xu Yougong, personal name Hongmin, avoided the taboo name of the Filial and Respectful Emperor and used his style in public; he was grandson of the National University Erudite Wenyuan.

units.zh: 舉明經，累補蒲州司法參軍，襲封東莞縣男。
units.en: He passed the Mingjing examination, served repeatedly as judicial aide in Puzhou, and inherited the barony of Dongguan.
units.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination, was repeatedly appointed Military Aide for Judicial Affairs in Puzhou, and inherited the enfeoffment as Baron of Dongguan.

units.zh: 為政仁，不忍杖罰，民服其恩，更相約曰：「犯徐參軍杖者，必斥之。」
units.en: He governed with benevolence and refused to use the rod. The people honored his kindness and agreed among themselves: "Whoever makes Staff Officer Xu use the rod will be driven out."
units.literal: His governance was benevolent; he could not bear corporal punishment; the people submitted to his kindness, and each other agreed, saying: "Whoever makes Staff Officer Xu beat with the rod must be driven out."

units.zh: 訖代不辱一人。
units.en: By the end of his term not one person had been beaten.
units.literal: By the end of his term not a single person had been shamed.

units.zh: 累遷司刑丞。
units.en: He was promoted repeatedly to vice director of the Court of Punishments.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Punishments.

units.zh: 時武後僭位，畏唐大臣謀己。
units.en: Empress Wu had seized the throne and feared plots from Tang ministers.
units.literal: At the time Empress Wu had usurped the throne and feared that Tang grand ministers would plot against her.

units.zh: 於是周興、來俊臣、丘神勣、王弘義等揣識後指，置總監牧院諸獄，捕將相，俾相鉤逮，掩搦護送，楚掠凝慘。
units.en: Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, Qiu Shenji, Wang Hongyi, and others divined her intent, set up the supervisory prison system, arrested ministers and generals, forced mutual denunciations, and tortured prisoners with savage cruelty.
units.literal: Thereupon Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, Qiu Shenji, Wang Hongyi, and others divined the empress's intent, established the general supervisory pasture-yard prisons, captured generals and chancellors, made them implicate and seize one another, cover and seize and escort, with torture cruel and congealed.

units.zh: 又汙引天下豪桀，馳使者即按，一切以反論。
units.en: They also implicated heroes across the empire; imperial envoys rushed to investigate, and every case was judged treason.
units.literal: They also defiled and implicated heroes throughout the realm; flying envoys immediately investigated on site, and all were judged as rebellion.

units.zh: 吏爭以周內窮詆相高，後輒勸以官賞，於是以急變相告言者無虛日。
units.en: Officials competed to extract confessions through torture; the empress rewarded them with offices, and accusations poured in daily without pause.
units.literal: Officials vied to be lofty in exhausting slander within the prisons; the empress always encouraged them with office rewards, and thus those who reported urgent changes had not a vacant day.

units.zh: 朝野震恐，莫敢正言，獨有功數犯顏爭枉直，後厲語折抑，有功爭益牢。
units.en: The court and countryside trembled with fear and none dared speak plainly. Only Yougong repeatedly defied the empress to argue right from wrong; though she rebuked him harshly, he held all the more firm.
units.literal: Court and countryside were shaken with fear; none dared speak uprightly. Only Yougong several times offended her countenance contending over wrong and right; the empress sternly rebuked and suppressed him, yet Yougong contended all the more firmly.

units.zh: 時博州刺史瑯邪王沖，責息錢於貴鄉，遣家奴督斂，與尉顏餘慶相聞知，奴自市弓矢還。
units.en: The prefect of Bozhou, Prince Chong of Langye, was collecting interest in Guixiang and sent a household slave to press payment. The assistant magistrate Yan Yuqing knew of this, and the slave bought bows and arrows on his own.
units.literal: At the time the Prefect of Bozhou, Prince Chong of Langye, was collecting interest money in Guixiang and sent a household slave to press collection; he had mutual knowledge with the Assistant Magistrate Yan Yuqing; the slave himself bought bows and arrows and returned.

units.zh: 會沖坐逆誅，魏州人告餘慶豫沖謀，後令俊臣鞫治，以反狀聞。
units.en: When Chong was executed for treason, men of Weizhou reported that Yuqing had foreknown the plot. The empress ordered Lai Junchen to investigate and reported a finding of treason.
units.literal: When Chong was executed for rebellion, people of Weizhou reported that Yuqing had foreknown Chong's plot; the empress ordered Junchen to investigate and try, reporting the circumstance of rebellion.

units.zh: 有司議：「餘慶更永昌赦，法當流。」
units.en: The responsible officials ruled: "Yuqing falls under the Yongchang amnesty and by law should be banished."
units.literal: The responsible officials deliberated: "Yuqing falls under the Yongchang amnesty and by law ought to be banished."

units.zh: 侍御史魏元忠謂：「餘慶為沖督償、通書，合謀明甚，非曰支黨，請殊死，籍其家。」
units.en: Attending Censor Wei Yuanzhong argued: "Yuqing collected debts for Chong and exchanged letters—the conspiracy is clear. He is no mere follower. I request execution and confiscation of his property."
units.literal: Attending Censor Wei Yuanzhong said: "Yuqing collected repayment for Chong and exchanged letters—the conspiracy is clearly evident; this is not called a branch party. I request extraordinary death and confiscation of his household."

units.zh: 詔可。
units.en: The edict approved.
units.literal: An edict approved.

units.zh: 有功曰：「永昌赦令：『與虺貞同惡，魁首已伏誅，支黨未發者原之。』
units.en: Yougong said, "The Yongchang amnesty states: 'Those who shared the guilt of Hui Zhen—since the ringleaders have been executed, followers not yet exposed are pardoned.'
units.literal: Yougong said: "The Yongchang amnesty order states: 'Those who shared evil with Hui Zhen—the ringleaders have already been executed; branch parties not yet exposed are pardoned.'

units.zh: 《書》曰：『殲厥渠魁』，律以『造意為首』，尋赦已伏語，則魁首無遺。
units.en: The Documents says, 'Destroy their chief ringleader,' and the law defines the originator as the head. Under the amnesty the ringleaders are already dead.
units.literal: The Documents says: 'Destroy their chief ringleader,' and the law takes 'the originator as head.' Seeking in the amnesty those already executed in speech, then the ringleaders leave none remaining.

units.zh: 餘慶赦後被言，是謂支黨。
units.en: Yuqing was accused only after the amnesty; he is therefore a follower.
units.literal: Yuqing was spoken of after the amnesty—this is called a branch party.

units.zh: 今以支為首，是以生入死。
units.en: To treat a follower as the ringleader is to condemn the living as if they were dead.
units.literal: Now to take a branch member as head is thereby to put the living into death.

units.zh: 赦而復罪，不如勿赦；
units.en: To pardon and then punish again is worse than never pardoning at all;
units.literal: To pardon and then again convict is not as good as not pardoning;

units.zh: 生而復殺，不如勿生。
units.en: to spare life and then kill is worse than never sparing at all.
units.literal: to give life and then again kill is not as good as not giving life.

units.zh: 竊謂朝廷不當爾。」
units.en: I submit that the court ought not act in this way."
units.literal: Your servant ventures to say the court ought not act thus."

units.zh: 后怒曰：「何謂魁首？」
units.en: The empress angrily asked, "What do you mean by ringleader?"
units.literal: The empress angrily said: "What is called ringleader?"

units.zh: 答曰：「魁者，大帥；
units.en: He answered, "Ringleader means the chief commander;
units.literal: He replied: "Ringleader means the great commander;

units.zh: 首者，元謀。」
units.en: head means the prime plotter."
units.literal: head means the prime plotter."

units.zh: 後曰：「餘慶安得不為魁首？」
units.en: The empress said, "How can Yuqing not be the ringleader?"
units.literal: The empress said: "How can Yuqing not be the ringleader?"

units.zh: 答曰：「若魁首者，虺貞是已。
units.en: He replied, "If there is a ringleader, it is Hui Zhen.
units.literal: He replied: "If there is a ringleader, Hui Zhen is the one.

units.zh: 既已伏誅，餘慶今方論罪，非支黨何？」
units.en: He has already been executed. Yuqing is now being judged for a separate offense—what is he if not a follower?"
units.literal: Already executed, Yuqing is now being judged for guilt—if not a branch party, what?"

units.zh: 后意解，乃曰：「公更思之。」
units.en: The empress relented and said, "Think on it again."
units.literal: The empress's mind eased, and she said: "Sir, think on it again."

units.zh: 遂免死。
units.en: Yuqing was spared death.
units.literal: Thereupon he was spared death.

units.zh: 當此時，左右及衛仗在廷陛者數百人，皆縮項不敢息，而有功氣定言詳，然不橈。
units.en: At that moment hundreds of attendants and guards on the palace steps shrank in silence, yet Yougong spoke calmly and in detail without yielding.
units.literal: At this time, attendants and guards in the hundreds on the court steps all shrank their necks and did not dare breathe; yet Yougong's spirit was settled and his words detailed, and he did not bend.

units.zh: 有韓紀孝者，受徐敬業偽官，前已物故，推事使顧仲琰籍其家，詔已報可。
units.en: Han Jixiao had accepted a post from Xu Jingye's rebel regime and was already dead. Investigating commissioner Gu Zhongyan was seizing his estate after imperial approval.
units.literal: There was one Han Jixiao who had accepted a false office from Xu Jingye and had already died; the investigating commissioner Gu Zhongyan was registering his household; the edict had already been reported as approved.

units.zh: 有功追議曰：「律，謀反者斬。
units.en: Yougong objected: "The law says rebels are beheaded.
units.literal: Yougong pursued the deliberation, saying: "The law: rebels are beheaded.

units.zh: 身亡即無斬法，無斬法則不得相緣。
units.en: When the person is dead the capital penalty no longer applies; without capital penalty there can be no linked punishment.
units.literal: When the person is dead there is no law of beheading; when there is no law of beheading, there can be no linked punishment.

units.zh: 所緣之人亡，則所因之罪減。」
units.en: When the principal offender is dead, the dependent offense is reduced."
units.literal: When the person linked to is dead, the crime that depends on him is reduced."

units.zh: 詔從之，皆以更赦免，如此獲宥者數十百姓。
units.en: The edict followed his view. All were spared under the next amnesty; dozens of households were saved in this way.
units.literal: An edict followed this; all were spared through the next amnesty; those who obtained pardon in this way numbered several tens of households.

units.zh: 累轉秋官郎中。
units.en: He was promoted repeatedly to director of the Autumn Office.
units.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Director of the Autumn Office.

units.zh: 鳳閣侍郎任知古、冬官尚書裴行本等七人被誣當死，後謂宰相曰：「古人以殺止殺，我今以恩止殺，就群公丐知古等，賜以再生，可乎？」
units.en: Phoenix Pavilion vice minister Ren Zhigu, Winter Office minister Pei Xingben, and seven others faced false charges of death. The empress told the chancellors, "The ancients stopped killing by killing; I now wish to stop killing by grace. I ask you to spare Zhigu and the others and give them life again—is that possible?"
units.literal: Phoenix Pavilion Vice Minister Ren Zhigu, Winter Office Minister Pei Xingben, and seven others were falsely accused and faced death; the empress told the chancellors: "The ancients used killing to stop killing; I now use grace to stop killing. From among the lords I beg Zhigu and the others and grant them renewed life—is it possible?"

units.zh: 俊臣、張知默固請如法，後不許。
units.en: Lai Junchen and Zhang Zhimou insisted on applying the law, but the empress refused.
units.literal: Junchen and Zhang Zhimou firmly requested according to law; the empress did not permit.

units.zh: 俊臣獨引行本更驗前罪。
units.en: Lai Junchen alone took Xingben back to reinvestigate earlier offenses.
units.literal: Junchen alone led Xingben back to verify prior crimes.

units.zh: 有功奏曰：「俊臣違陛下再生之賜，不可以示信。」
units.en: Yougong memorialized, "Lai Junchen violates Your Majesty's grant of renewed life and cannot be trusted."
units.literal: Yougong memorialized, saying: "Junchen violates Your Majesty's gift of renewed life and cannot be shown as trustworthy."

units.zh: 於是悉免死。
units.en: All were then spared death.
units.literal: Thereupon all were spared death.

units.zh: 道州刺史李仁褒兄弟為人誣構，有功爭不能得。
units.en: Li Renbao and his brothers of Daozhou were falsely accused, and Yougong argued in vain.
units.literal: Li Renbao and his brothers, prefect of Daozhou, were falsely framed by others; Yougong contended but could not prevail.

units.zh: 秋官侍郎周興劾之曰：「漢法，附下罔上者斬，面欺者亦斬。
units.en: Autumn Office vice minister Zhou Xing impeached him: "Han law beheads those who mislead superiors and deceive subordinates, and also those who deceive the throne to its face.
units.literal: Autumn Office Vice Minister Zhou Xing impeached him, saying: "Han law: those who deceive superiors and mislead subordinates are beheaded; those who deceive to the face are also beheaded.

units.zh: 在古，析言破律者殺。
units.en: In antiquity those who twisted the law with clever words were executed.
units.literal: In antiquity, those who twisted words to break the law were killed.

units.zh: 有功故出反囚，罪當誅，請按之。」
units.en: Yougong deliberately released rebel prisoners and deserves death. I ask that he be prosecuted."
units.literal: Yougong deliberately released rebel prisoners; the crime deserves execution—please investigate."

units.zh: 後不許，猶坐史官。
units.en: The empress refused but still demoted him to a historiographer post.
units.literal: The empress did not permit it but still punished him as a historiographer.

units.zh: 俄起為左肅政臺侍御史，辭曰：「臣聞鹿走山林而命系庖廚者，勢固自然。
units.en: He was soon appointed attending censor of the Left Office for Correcting Governance. He declined: "I have heard that when a deer runs in the mountains yet its life hangs on the kitchen, that is only the way of nature.
units.literal: Soon he was raised as Attending Censor of the Left Office for Correcting Governance; he declined, saying: "Your servant has heard that when a deer runs in mountain forests yet its life hangs on the kitchen, the situation is solid and natural.

units.zh: 陛下以法官用臣，臣守正行法，必坐此死矣。」
units.en: Your Majesty appoints me as a judge. If I uphold the law uprightly I will surely die for it."
units.literal: Your Majesty employs your servant as a judge; your servant upholds the law with integrity and will surely sit in this crime unto death."

units.zh: 後固授之。
units.en: The empress insisted on appointing him.
units.literal: The empress firmly invested him.

units.zh: 天下聞有功復進，灑然相賀。
units.en: When the empire heard Yougong had returned to office, people rejoiced throughout the land.
units.literal: When all under Heaven heard Yougong had returned to office, they rejoiced and congratulated one another.

units.zh: 時有詔：「公坐流、私坐徒以上會赦免，逾百日不首者，復論。」
units.en: An edict then stated: "For public crimes of exile and private crimes of penal servitude and above, if pardoned by amnesty, those who do not surrender within a hundred days will be prosecuted again."
units.literal: At the time there was an edict: "For public crimes exile and private crimes penal servitude and above, if pardoned by amnesty, those who after a hundred days do not surrender are again prosecuted."

units.zh: 有功奏曰：「陛下寬殊死罪，已發者原之，是通改過之心、自新之路。
units.en: Yougong memorialized: "Your Majesty has widened mercy for capital crimes and pardoned those already exposed. This opens the way to repentance and renewal.
units.literal: Yougong memorialized, saying: "Your Majesty has widened crimes deserving extraordinary death; those already exposed are pardoned—this opens the heart to reform faults and the road to renew oneself.

units.zh: 故律，告赦前事，以其罪坐之。
units.en: The law therefore punishes reporting pre-amnesty offenses.
units.literal: Therefore the law: reporting matters before the amnesty seats guilt on the crime.

units.zh: 若無告言，所犯終不自發；
units.en: Without a report the offense would never come to light;
units.literal: If there is no report, the offense in the end will not expose itself;

units.zh: 如告言赦前事，則與律乖。
units.en: yet reporting pre-amnesty offenses contradicts the law.
units.literal: if one reports matters before the amnesty, then it departs from the law.

units.zh: 今赦前之罪，不自言者，還以法論，即恩雖布天下，而一罪不能貸，臣竊為陛下不取。」
units.en: Now those who do not confess pre-amnesty crimes are still punished. Though grace covers the empire, a single offense cannot be forgiven. I submit that Your Majesty should not accept this."
units.literal: Now for crimes before the amnesty, those who do not speak of themselves are still judged by law—then though grace is spread through all under Heaven, one crime cannot be forgiven; your servant ventures to say Your Majesty ought not take this."

units.zh: 後更詔五品以上議可。
units.en: The empress ordered officials of fifth rank and above to deliberate and approve.
units.literal: The empress again ordered officials of fifth rank and above to deliberate and approve.

units.zh: 又上疏曰：「天下員有定，比選者日多，選曹諉囑公行，囂謗滿路。
units.en: He also memorialized: "Posts throughout the realm have fixed quotas, yet candidates for selection grow daily. The Selection Office evades duty while patronage runs openly, and complaint fills the roads.
units.literal: He also submitted a memorial, saying: "Posts throughout the realm have fixed quotas, yet those competing in selection grow daily; the Selection Office shirks responsibility while patronage runs openly, and slander fills the roads.

units.zh: 唐季人多逆節，鞫訊結斷，刑慘獄嚴，革命歲久，其流弗改。
units.en: Under the Tang many had turned against proper conduct; trials ended in cruel punishments and harsh prisons. Though the dynasty had long been secure, those practices had not changed.
units.literal: In the Tang age many turned against proper conduct; inquisition, judgment, and sentencing ended with cruel punishments and severe prisons; though the revolution had long passed, its current did not change.

units.zh: 事表生情，法外構理，而刻薄吏驅扇成奸。
units.en: Cases were built on appearances and feelings; officials constructed guilt beyond the law, and harsh magistrates drove wrongdoing into conspiracy.
units.literal: Affairs appeared on the surface and feeling arose; outside the law reason was constructed, while harsh officials drove and fanned wrongdoing into treachery.

units.zh: 雖朝堂進表，列匭內牒，叫閽弗聽，叩鼓弗聞，使申其冤，正增其枉。
units.en: Though memorials reached the morning court and petitions were placed in the complaint boxes, cries at the gate went unheard and drum appeals unanswered, so that seeking justice only deepened injustice.
units.literal: Though memorials were advanced in the morning court and petitions placed in the boxes within, crying at the gate was not heard and beating the drum was not listened to—making them declare their grievance only increased their wrong.

units.zh: 誠令天官銓註有所不平、法司推斷舞法深詆、三司理匭受所上章擁塞不白者皆許臣按驗劾發，奪祿貶勞，不越月逾時，可致刑措。」
units.en: If Your Majesty permits me to investigate unfair selections, corrupt judgments, and blocked grievance petitions, to impeach offenders and strip their salaries and rank, within a month the realm could reach a state where punishments fall unused."
units.literal: Truly, if wherever the Celestial Office's selection annotations are unfair, wherever the law office's judgments twist the law with deep slander, and wherever the Three Offices handling the accusation box receive submitted memorials but block and do not report them—all are permitted your servant to investigate, verify, impeach, and expose, stripping salary and degrading evaluation—within no more than a month or season, punishments may be set aside unused."

units.zh: 后納之。
units.en: The empress accepted his proposal.
units.literal: The empress accepted this.

units.zh: 竇孝諶妻龐為其奴怖以妖祟，教為夜解，因告以厭詛。
units.en: Dou Xiaochen's wife Pang was terrorized by a slave who claimed she was possessed, taught her secret night rites, then accused her of curse-magic.
units.literal: Dou Xiaochen's wife Pang was frightened by her slave with talk of demonic portents; the slave taught her to perform night rites of release and then reported her for curse-magic.

units.zh: 給事中薛季昶鞫之，龐當死。
units.en: Supervising Secretary Xue Jichang tried the case, and Pang faced execution.
units.literal: Supervising Secretary Xue Jichang tried the case; Pang was liable to death.

units.zh: 子希瑊訟冤，有功明其枉。
units.en: Her son Xi Huang appealed the injustice, and Yougong proved her innocence.
units.literal: Her son Xi Huang sued for injustice; Yougong clarified her wrongful conviction.

units.zh: 季昶劾有功黨惡逆，當棄市。
units.en: Jichang impeached Yougong for siding with rebels and demanded his public execution.
units.literal: Jichang impeached Yougong for siding with evil rebels and deserving execution in the marketplace.

units.zh: 有功方視事，令史泣以告。
units.en: Yougong was at his desk when a clerk wept to tell him the news.
units.literal: Yougong was just attending to business when a clerk wept to inform him.

units.zh: 有功曰：「豈吾獨死，而諸人長不死邪？」
units.en: Yougong said, "Do you think I alone must die while the rest of you will live forever?"
units.literal: Yougong said: "Is it that I alone must die while you gentlemen will long not die?"

units.zh: 安步去。
units.en: He walked away calmly.
units.literal: He walked away at ease.

units.zh: 後召詰曰：「公比斷獄多失出，何耶？」
units.en: The empress later summoned him and asked, "You often release prisoners improperly. Why?"
units.literal: Later the empress summoned and interrogated him, saying: "Sir, you often err in releasing prisoners—why?"

units.zh: 對曰：「失出，臣小過；
units.en: He answered, "Releasing the wrongly accused is my small fault;
units.literal: He replied: "Erring in release is your servant's small fault;

units.zh: 好生，陛下大德。」
units.en: cherishing life is Your Majesty's great virtue."
units.literal: cherishing life is Your Majesty's great virtue."

units.zh: 後默然。
units.en: The empress fell silent.
units.literal: The empress was silent.

units.zh: 龐得減死，有功免為民。
units.en: Pang's sentence was commuted from death, and Yougong was reduced to commoner status.
units.literal: Pang's sentence was reduced from death; Yougong was dismissed to commoner status.

units.zh: 起拜左司郎中，轉司刑少卿。
units.en: He was restored as director of the Left Office and promoted to vice minister of the Court of Punishments.
units.literal: He was raised and appointed Director of the Left Office; transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Punishments.

units.zh: 與皇甫文備同按獄，誣有功縱逆黨。
units.en: Investigating cases with Huangfu Wenbei, he was falsely accused by Wenbei of releasing rebel partisans.
units.literal: Together with Huangfu Wenbei he investigated cases; Wenbei falsely accused Yougong of releasing rebel partisans.

units.zh: 久之，文備坐事下獄，有功出之。
units.en: Later Wenbei was imprisoned for an offense, and Yougong secured his release.
units.literal: After a long time Wenbei was imprisoned for an offense; Yougong released him.

units.zh: 或曰：「彼嘗陷君於死，今生之，何也？」
units.en: Someone asked, "He once tried to have you killed. Why save him now?"
units.literal: Someone said: "He once trapped you in death; now you give him life—why?"

units.zh: 對曰：「爾所言者私忿，我所守者公法，不可以私害公。」
units.en: He replied, "That is private resentment. I uphold public law, and private feeling cannot harm the public good."
units.literal: He replied: "What you speak of is private resentment; what I uphold is public law—private feeling cannot harm public law."

units.zh: 嘗謂所親曰：「大理，人命所系，不可阿旨詭辭，以求茍免。」
units.en: He once told his intimates, "The Ministry of Punishments holds human lives in its hands. One cannot twist words to flatter superiors and escape responsibility."
units.literal: Once he told those close to him: "The Ministry of Punishments is what human lives depend on; one cannot flatter intent with deceitful words to seek careless escape."

units.zh: 故有功為獄，常持平守正，以執據冤罔，凡三坐大辟，將死，泰然不憂，赦之，亦不喜，後以此重之。
units.en: In every case he judged, he held to the middle way and relied on evidence against wrongful imprisonment. Three times he faced execution and met death calmly; when pardoned he showed no joy. For this the court esteemed him all the more.
units.literal: Therefore when Yougong conducted prisons he always held the mean and guarded rectitude, relying on evidence against wrongful imprisonment; altogether three times he faced great execution, about to die yet calm without worry; when pardoned he was not pleased either—later for this he was highly regarded.

units.zh: 所全活甚眾，酷吏為少衰，然疾之如仇矣。
units.en: He saved a great many lives, and the cruel officials somewhat relented, though they hated him as an enemy.
units.literal: Those he preserved alive were very many; cruel officials somewhat declined, yet they hated him as an enemy.

units.zh: 改司仆少卿。
units.en: He was made vice minister of the Court of Equine Administration.
units.literal: He was changed to Vice Minister of the Court of Equine Administration.

units.zh: 卒，年六十八，贈司刑卿。
units.en: He died at sixty-eight and was posthumously honored as Minister of Punishments.
units.literal: He died at age sixty-eight and was posthumously given Minister of Punishments.

units.zh: 中宗即位，加贈越州都督，遣使就第吊祭，賜物百段，授一子官。
units.en: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne he was posthumously made governor of Yuezhou; envoys mourned at his home, bestowed a hundred lengths of goods, and granted office to one son.
units.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne he was further given Governor of Yuezhou; envoys were sent to his residence for mourning sacrifice, a hundred lengths of goods bestowed, and one son granted office.

units.zh: 開元初，竇希瑊等請以己官讓有功子惀，以報舊德，由是自大理司直遷恭陵令。
units.en: Early in Kaiyuan, Dou Xi Huang and others asked to yield their offices to Yougong's son Lun in repayment of his kindness, and Lun rose from straightener in the Ministry of Punishments to magistrate of Gongling.
units.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, Dou Xi Huang and others requested to yield their own offices to Yougong's son Lun in repayment of old grace; thereby from Straightener of the Ministry of Punishments he was moved to Magistrate of Gongling.

units.zh: 會昌中，追謚忠正。
units.en: In the Huichang era he was posthumously titled Loyal and Upright.
units.literal: In the Huichang era he was posthumously given the title Loyal and Upright.

units.zh: 初，鹿城主簿潘好禮慕有功為人，論之曰：「昔稱張釋之為廷尉，天下無冤人，今有功斷獄，亦天下無冤人。
units.en: Earlier Pan Haoli, chief clerk of Lucheng, praised Yougong: "People once said that when Zhang Shizhi was minister of punishments there were no wronged persons under Heaven. Under Yougong there were likewise none.
units.literal: Earlier, Pan Haoli, chief clerk of Lucheng, admired Yougong's character and discussed him, saying: "Former times praised Zhang Shizhi as Minister of Punishments, and under Heaven there were no wronged persons; now Yougong's judgments of prisoners also mean under Heaven there are no wronged persons.

units.zh: 然釋之當漢文帝時，中外無事，守法而已。
units.en: But Shizhi served Emperor Wen of Han when the realm was at peace and he needed only to uphold the law.
units.literal: Yet Shizhi was in the time of Emperor Wen of Han, when inside and outside were without affairs and he only guarded the law.

units.zh: 有功居革命之際，周興、來俊臣等掩義隱賊，崇飾惡言，以誣盛德，有功守死明道，身濱殆者數矣，此其賢於釋之明甚。」
units.en: Yougong lived in an age of revolution, when Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others concealed villains and twisted words to slander the throne. He held to the Way even at the risk of death, several times on the brink of execution. In this he far surpassed Shizhi."
units.literal: Yougong dwelt in the age of revolution; Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others covered righteousness and hid villains, adorned evil words to slander sagely virtue; Yougong guarded death to clarify the Way, his person several times on the brink of peril—this shows his surpassing Shizhi in clarity."

units.zh: 或稱有功仁恕過漢於、張。
units.en: Some said Yougong's benevolence and forbearance surpassed the celebrated Han judges Yu Dingguo and Zhang Shizhi.
units.literal: Some called Yougong's benevolence and forbearance superior to the Yu and Zhang of Han.

units.zh: 起居舍人盧若虛曰：「徐公當雷霆之震，而能全仁恕，雖千載未見其比。」
units.en: Diary attendant Lu Ruoxu said, "Minister Xu preserved benevolence and forbearance even amid thunderous terror. In a thousand years his like has not been seen."
units.literal: Diary Attendant Lu Ruoxu said: "Minister Xu, amid thunderous shocks, could yet preserve benevolence and forbearance—though a thousand years have passed, his like has not been seen."

units.zh: 五世孫商。
units.en: His fifth-generation descendant was Shang.
units.literal: A fifth-generation descendant was Shang.

units.zh: 贊曰：「徐有功不以唐、周貳其心，惟一於法，身蹈死以救人之死，故能處猜後、酷吏之間，以恕自將，內挫虐焰，不使天下殘於燎，可謂仁人也哉！
units.en: The commentator writes: "Xu Yougong never divided his loyalty between Tang and Zhou. He held only to the law and risked his own life to save others. Amid suspicion and cruel officials he governed through forbearance, checked their cruelty inwardly, and kept the realm from being consumed by fire. He may truly be called a benevolent man!
units.literal: The encomium says: "Xu Yougong did not divide his heart between Tang and Zhou; he held only to the law, personally treading death to save others from death; therefore he could dwell among suspicion afterward and cruel officials, taking forbearance as his guide, inwardly checking cruel flames so that the realm was not maimed by the blaze—he may be called a benevolent man!

units.zh: 議者謂過漢於、張，渠不信夫！」
units.en: Those who say he surpassed the Yu and Zhang of Han—who can doubt it!"
units.literal: Those who discuss say he surpassed the Yu and Zhang of Han—how can one not believe it!"

units.zh: 商，字義聲，或字秋卿，客新鄭再世，因為新鄭人。
units.en: Shang, whose style was Yisheng or Qiuqing, came from a family that had lived in Xinzheng for two generations and thus became a native of that place.
units.literal: Shang, style name Yisheng, or style name Qiuqing, his family having lodged in Xinzheng for two generations, thus became a man of Xinzheng.

units.zh: 幼隱中條山。
units.en: In youth he lived in seclusion on Mount Zhongtiao.
units.literal: In youth he hid on Mount Zhongtiao.

units.zh: 擢進士第。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination.
units.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.

units.zh: 大中時，擢累尚書左丞。
units.en: During the Dazhong reign he rose by successive promotions to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: In the Dazhong era he was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 宣宗詔為巡邊使，使有指，拜河中節度使。
units.en: Emperor Xuanzong appointed him border-touring commissioner, and when his mission succeeded he became military commissioner of Hezhong.
units.literal: Emperor Xuanzong ordered him border-touring commissioner; when his mission had purpose, he was appointed Military Commissioner of Hezhong.

units.zh: 突厥殘種保特峨山，以千帳度河自歸，詔商綏定。
units.en: Remnant Turks held Mount E with a thousand tents and crossed the river to submit. The emperor ordered Shang to settle them.
units.literal: Remnant Turks held Mount E in protection; with a thousand tents they crossed the river to submit; an edict ordered Shang to pacify and settle them.

units.zh: 商表處山東寬鄉，置備征軍，凡千人，襞紙為鎧，勁矢不能洞。
units.en: Shang settled them east of the mountains in Kuandxiang and formed a thousand-man reserve army whose pleated-paper armor strong arrows could not pierce.
units.literal: Shang memorialized to place them in Kuandxiang east of the mountains, establishing a prepared campaign army of a thousand men; pleated paper served as armor, and strong arrows could not pierce it.

units.zh: 徙節山南東道，襄多山棚，為票賊，商取材卒為捕盜將，別為屯營，寇所發，輒跡捕，捕必得，遂為精兵。
units.en: Transferred to eastern Shannan, where mountain bandits were numerous, he selected tough soldiers as anti-bandit troops in separate camps. Whenever raiders struck he tracked them down and always captured them, forging an elite force.
units.literal: He moved his headquarters to the eastern route of Shannan; Xiang had many mountain sheds and bandit raiders; Shang selected material soldiers as bandit-capture generals, separately encamped; wherever raiders struck he tracked and seized them, capture was certain, and they became crack troops.

units.zh: 江西都將反，韋宙乘傳抵山南發兵，商命部將韓季友以捕盜營士往。
units.en: When the Jiangxi military commissioner rebelled, Wei Zhou rushed to Shannan to raise troops, and Shang sent his general Han Jiyou with the anti-bandit battalion.
units.literal: The Jiangxi military commissioner rebelled; Wei Zhou traveled by post to Shannan to raise troops; Shang ordered his subordinate general Han Jiyou to lead the bandit-capture camp soldiers there.

units.zh: 賊平，宙表留季友所部為綱紀。
units.en: After the rebellion was crushed, Wei Zhou kept Jiyou's unit as garrison troops.
units.literal: When the rebels were pacified, Zhou memorialized to retain Jiyou's command as discipline troops.

units.zh: 咸通初，以刑部尚書為諸道鹽鐵轉運使，封東莞縣子。
units.en: Early in Xiantong he became Minister of Punishments and salt-and-iron transport commissioner for all circuits, and was enfeoffed Viscount of Dongguan.
units.literal: Early in Xiantong he was Minister of Punishments and commissioner for salt and iron transport on all circuits, enfeoffed as Viscount of Dongguan.

units.zh: 四年，進同中書門下平章事，出為荊南節度使。
units.en: In the fourth year he became chancellor and was posted as military commissioner of Jingnan.
units.literal: In the fourth year he advanced to Same Rank as the Three Offices of the Secretariat and Chancellery and went out as Military Commissioner of Jingnan.

units.zh: 累進太子太保，卒。
units.en: He rose to junior tutor of the heir apparent and died.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and died.

units.zh: 子彥若，事僖宗為中書舍人。
units.en: His son Yanruo served Emperor Xizong as secretariat drafting officer.
units.literal: His son Yanruo served Emperor Xizong as Drafting Officer of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 昭宗立，再用為御史中丞。
units.en: When Emperor Zhaozong took the throne, Yanruo twice served as censor-in-chief.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong took the throne, he was twice used as Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 張浚師敗太原，以彥若為戶部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
units.en: After Zhang Jun's defeat at Taiyuan, Yanruo was made vice minister of revenue and chancellor.
units.literal: When Zhang Jun's army was defeated at Taiyuan, Yanruo was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Same Rank as the Three Offices of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

units.zh: 俄代李茂貞為鳳翔節度使，不得入，還為御史大夫。
units.en: He soon replaced Li Maozhen as military commissioner of Fengxiang but could not take up the post and returned as grand master of the censorate.
units.literal: Soon he replaced Li Maozhen as Military Commissioner of Fengxiang but could not enter; he returned as Grand Master of the Censorate.

units.zh: 乾寧初，復當國，進位太保、齊國公。
units.en: Early in Qianning he again directed the government, rising to Grand Guardian and Duke of Qi.
units.literal: Early in Qianning he again held state power, advanced to Grand Guardian and Duke of Qi.

units.zh: 崔胤專政，以彥若位己右，不悅，以平章事為清海軍節度使，卒於鎮，而行軍司馬劉隱因主留務。
units.en: Cui Yin dominated the government and, resenting Yanruo's senior rank, sent him to the Qinghai Army circuit as military commissioner in place of the chancellorship. He died in office, and the acting officer Liu Yin seized control of affairs.
units.literal: Cui Yin monopolized government; because Yanruo stood above him he was displeased and made Yanruo Military Commissioner of the Qinghai Army in place of his chancellorship; he died in the prefecture, and the acting military affairs officer Liu Yin seized control of remaining duties.

units.zh: 方時多難，彥若最見信於帝，有以事自陳者，帝曰：「汝當問彥若。」
units.en: In those troubled times Yanruo was the emperor's most trusted minister. When anyone came with a private petition the emperor said, "Ask Yanruo."
units.literal: At a time of many hardships Yanruo was most trusted by the emperor; when someone presented a matter in his own interest the emperor said: "You should ask Yanruo."

units.zh: 其所倚任如此。
units.en: Such was the reliance the emperor placed on him.
units.literal: Such was the reliance placed on him.
